## Claims
- [source-backed] The lower-adjoined family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) generates \(J_v\); the cited theorem proves its minimality. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235]
- [source-backed] For every valid \((n,r,i,j,a,b,N)\), no nonzero homogeneous syzygy of the lower-adjoined form exists. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 270-304, 819-825]
- [proved] Let \(q=n-r\), \(p=q-i\), \(c=r-j\), and
  \[
  v^\vee=v_{q,\;q+j-i,\;q-i+1,\;n}.
  \]
  Then \(v^\vee\) is bigrassmannian, its parameters are
  \[
  (i^\vee,j^\vee,a^\vee,b^\vee)=(j,i,a,b),
  \]
  and
  \[
  J_v/A_+J_v\cong
  \bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})}
  \mathbb Z[\bar s_\mu].
  \]
  Hence \(G_R\) is an integral homogeneous basis of indecomposables, is an irredundant generating family of \(J_v\), and
  \[
  \operatorname{Hilb}_{J_v/A_+J_v}(z)
  =z^{ij}\binom{a+b}{a}_z.
  \]

## Strategy
The requested right-adjoined indecomposables theorem is established, using the accepted admissibility and quotient-conjugation certificates.

Put \(q=n-r\), \(p=q-i\), and \(c=r-j\). Bigrassmannian admissibility gives \(p,c\geq0\). For
\[
(r^\vee,s^\vee,t^\vee)=(q,q+j-i,q-i+1)=(q,j+p,p+1),
\]
one has
\[
1\le p+1\le q,\qquad p+1\le j+p,\qquad
p+1>q+(j+p)-n=p-c.
\]
Thus \(v^\vee\) is admissible. Directly,
\[
i^\vee=s^\vee-t^\vee+1=j,\quad
j^\vee=r^\vee-t^\vee+1=i,
\]
and
\[
a^\vee=\min(r-j,q-i)=\min(c,p)=a,\qquad b^\vee=b.
\]

By the accepted quotient-conjugation certificate, partition conjugation induces a graded integral isomorphism
\[
\Omega:J_v/A_+J_v\xrightarrow{\sim}J_{v^\vee}/A_+J_{v^\vee},
\qquad [\bar s_\lambda]\mapsto[\bar s_{\lambda'}].
\]
If
\[
\lambda=(i+\alpha_1,\ldots,i+\alpha_b,i^{\,j-b}),
\qquad \alpha\subseteq a^b,
\]
then
\[
\lambda'=(j^i,\alpha').
\]
Since \(\alpha'\subseteq b^a\), \(\Omega\) bijects \(G_R\) with the lower-adjoined family for \(v^\vee\).

For \(a\ge1\), the transformed parameters satisfy the source’s validity inequalities, so the cited no-syzygy theorem shows that the lower-adjoined residues are \(\mathbb Z\)-independent modulo \(A_+J_{v^\vee}\). They span because that family generates \(J_{v^\vee}\). For \(a=0\), the family is the singleton \(\{\bar s_{j^i}\}\), lying in the least nonzero degree of the ideal, hence is likewise a basis of indecomposables. Applying \(\Omega^{-1}\) proves the displayed integral basis statement for \(G_R\).

Finally, \(\alpha\mapsto\alpha'\) gives
\[
\sum_{\mu\in G_R}z^{|\mu|}
=z^{ij}\sum_{\rho\subseteq b^a}z^{|\rho|}
=z^{ij}\binom{a+b}{a}_z,
\qquad
\binom{a+b}{a}_z=\prod_{u=1}^{a}\frac{1-z^{b+u}}{1-z^u}.
\]
For \(a=0\), this is \(z^{ij}\).

## Gaps
None under the stipulated accepted admissibility and quotient-conjugation certificates.
